title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the notes concern dévissage of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes and multiplicative structures. The surrounding pages set up an abstract framework. There is a category P whose objects are k-modules, or Modules over a ringed topos. Its morphism sets P(X,Y) carry gradings P_ν by polynomial degree, so that 'k-polynomial maps homogeneous of degree ν' behave like a graded k-linear structure. The previous page calls this a '(co-)pd-category', with the category of k-modules as the basic example. It ends by asking whether Γ^*(M) carries a pd-type structure, i.e. maps Γ^p(Γ^q M) → Γ^{pq} M satisfying the divided-power axioms.

This page, step by step:
(1) In the abstract setting there is an analogous extra structure on composition. The composition P(X,Y) × P(Y,Z) → P(X,Z), (f,g) ↦ g∘f, is k-linear in g, the second argument. It should be repackaged as a k-linear map
  P(Y,Z) → PolMap_k(P(X,Y), P(X,Z)),
sending g to the k-polynomial map f ↦ g∘f. If g has degree ν, then f ↦ g∘f is homogeneous of degree ν.
(2) This analysis is already available in the principal example, i.e. polynomial maps between modules, where it is just Roby's theory of polynomial laws.
(3) The construction should therefore reduce essentially to equipping the divided-power functors Γ^p with this extra structure. For all X, Y, the assignment
  f ↦ Γ^p(f) : Hom_1(X,Y) → Hom_1(Γ^p X, Γ^p Y)
must be given as a polynomial map (polynomial law) of degree p between the k-modules Hom_1(X,Y) and Hom_1(Γ^pX, Γ^pY). Here Hom_1 means degree-1, i.e. linear, morphisms. It must not be merely a set-theoretic map.

In modern terms, this is precisely the requirement that Γ^p be a strict polynomial functor of degree p in the sense of Friedlander–Suslin: the action on Hom-modules is a homogeneous polynomial law of degree p, equivalently a linear map Γ^p Hom(X,Y) → Hom(Γ^pX, Γ^pY). Such a functorial polynomial structure is what is needed to make sense of plethysm-type maps Γ^p∘Γ^q → Γ^{pq} and pd-structures in a categorical, sheafified, base-change-stable way, rather than pointwise on elements. The page, the last of the folder, breaks off mid-sentence.
errors: No mathematical error. The text is a programme statement, not a proof, and it is unfinished: the page (85/85) ends mid-sentence, and the requested pd-structure Γ^p(Γ^q M) → Γ^{pq} M and its compatibility axioms are never constructed here.
Minor ambiguity: 'Hom_1' is not defined on this page; it presumably denotes the degree-1 (linear) component of P(X,Y). The degree index switches between n and p.

ideas.what: Category whose Hom-sets are k-modules with composition k-linear in one variable and polynomial in the other, recast as a linear map P(Y,Z) → PolMap(P(X,Y), P(X,Z)).
ideas.modern_name: Category enriched in polynomial laws; closest notions are the categories Γ^dV used to define strict polynomial functors, and polynomial/analytic enrichment
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby (polynomial laws, 1963); Friedlander–Suslin (1997) for the Γ^d-enriched category formalism

ideas.what: Requirement that f ↦ Γ^p(f) on Hom-modules be a homogeneous polynomial law of degree p, not just a map of sets.
ideas.modern_name: Strict polynomial functor of degree p (equivalently a linear map Γ^p Hom(X,Y) → Hom(Γ^pX, Γ^pY))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Friedlander–Suslin 1997 (anticipated by Roby 1963 and by Eilenberg–MacLane/Bousfield-type polynomial functors)

ideas.what: Using this functorial polynomial structure to define pd-type plethysm structures Γ^p∘Γ^q → Γ^{pq} in an abstract or topos setting, as input to multiplicative structures on perfect complexes.
ideas.modern_name: Plethysm of divided powers / divided power structure on Γ^+(M) (Roby 1965); derived divided powers and derived pd-structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby (1965); Berthelot; later derived versions by Illusie and by Brantner–Mathew, among others

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes axiomatizing '(co-)pd-categories': categories with polynomially graded Hom-modules, composition linear in one variable and polynomial in the other. He also proposes requiring the functors Γ^p to act by degree-p polynomial laws on Hom-modules, so that pd-type structures Γ^pΓ^q → Γ^{pq} can be built abstractly over a ringed topos. The thread stops mid-sentence at the end of the folder.
missed.quote: f ↦ Γ^p(f) : Hom_1(X,Y) → Hom_1(Γ^p X, Γ^p Y) doit être défini comme "application pol. de degré p" ... et non seulement comme application ensembliste
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates, by about 20 years, the defining condition of strict polynomial functors (Friedlander–Suslin 1997). It does so inside a categorical framework (a polynomially enriched category over a topos) aimed at multiplicative structures on perfect complexes. Such a framework connects to current work on derived divided powers and polynomial monads, but no general 'pd-category' axiomatics of this kind seems to be standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The key idea is that Γ^p must act on Hom-modules as a degree-p polynomial law, and that composition should be packaged as linear-to-polynomial maps. This is essentially the strict-polynomial-functor viewpoint, appearing in the mid-1970s within a programme on perfect complexes. It is a notable anticipation, but it is only stated as a desideratum. Roby's polynomial laws were already available, and the thread is unfinished, so specialist surprise is moderate.
transcription_corrections: 'dans le cas de l'exemple en outre[?]' should likely read 'dans le cas de l'exemple abstrait:' (cf. 'cas "abstrait"' on the previous page).
'(multilinéaire[?] en le dernier argument[?])' more likely reads '(k-linéaire en le deuxième argument)'. This is consistent with composition being linear in g ∈ P(Y,Z).
'La construction doit se résumer' likely 'doit se ramener'.
'(étant[?] les modules' likely '(étant donnés les modules'.
The crossed-out 'Hom_P' before the composition formula carries a subscript that may be 'P' or 'p'.
'(Appl. k-polynomiales)(P(X,Y), P(X,Z))' is correct; the final argument is partly cut off at the margin.
